evidence.text: The FY2026/2027 outlook given on 23 September has to lap three things that do not repeat: a ~EUR 30m one-off from the sale of licensing rights tied to the North American corn divestiture, a EUR 7.7m participation gain from selling the AgReliant JV stakes, and the AgReliant equity income itself - on top of a Russian business [THE COMPANY] says is still shrinking. evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guidance line is where this stock's biggest moves have come from. 2026-02-12, comparable sales guidance cut from ~3% to flat with the margin band held: -7.42%. 2025-02-13, the equivalent H1 guidance event a year earlier: -9.49%. 2025-09-25, FY24/25 results setting the 3% FY25/26 guide plus the new three-year 3-5% / 19-21% medium-term frame: -3.13%. All three negative, and the two that changed a number were the two largest.
evidence.why_not_priced: The English-language record carries the EUR 29m one-off as a line in the 9M release but not the second item - the EUR 7.7m participation gain - and nowhere joins them to the FY26/27 base. The AgReliant divestiture ad-hoc of 2025-06-27 quantified the proceeds only as 'a low three-digit million range (USD)'; there is no public number for the equity income [THE COMPANY] loses with it. With five analysts and no published note since 20.07.2026, nobody has walked the market through an FY26/27 EBITDA base that is roughly EUR 30m lower before a single operating assumption is made. If this were priced, the stock would not be trading 2.6% off its high into the release, and the July target raise (78->85) would have been accompanied by a cut to FY26/27 estimates.

evidence.text: The 2027 German sugarbeet contracting round is already settled and it came out BETTER than the two preceding years, which [THE COMPANY] can underwrite in its FY26/27 outlook: the SZVG - the growers' cooperative that holds the majority stake in Suedzucker - has released 100% of delivery rights for the 2027 cultivation contract, cancelling the 90% restriction imposed in spring, explicitly because of the expected fall in sugar output from the 2026 harvest. Sugarbeet is EUR 324.6m of [THE COMPANY]'s EUR 386.8m 9M group EBITDA, and European beet seed is billed in the Jan-Mar quarter that sits inside FY26/27.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean precedent: [THE COMPANY] has guided European beet acreage DOWN at each of its last three releases and the stock fell each time (-3.13%, -7.42%, -2.31%). There is no observation in the last two years of [THE COMPANY] guiding beet area up, so this is the first time the segment narrative could turn and the reaction is unmodelled - which is the argument for a real but bounded positive rather than a large one.
evidence.why_not_priced: The English-language coverage of EU sugar in August and September 2026 is entirely about the PRICE and the CROP - NW European sugar at EUR 550/t on 3 September, +40% year to date, EU 2026/27 output cut to a 38-year low - and says nothing about the contracting decisions that actually set how much beet seed [THE COMPANY] sells. Those decisions live on a German growers' cooperative website and in the German farm press, in German, and they are the transmission mechanism. If the market had read them, the sell-side would have a published FY26/27 European beet-volume assumption, and there is no note on the name since 20.07.2026. Sized small deliberately, for three reasons the same German sources give: the SZVG decision covers southern Germany only, a fraction of [THE COMPANY]'s global beet seed book; Nordzucker's agreed 2027 minimum price is EUR 31.00/t, below prior years; and Pfeifer & Langen has cut more than 80 growers with ~1,200 ha out of 2027 contracts altogether. This is a direct counterparty in the beet chain speaking, not [THE COMPANY], so it is a hypothesis about [THE COMPANY]'s guidance until [THE COMPANY] says it.
